scope: Proposition 3.5 (Stationary-aspect profile) of the manuscript “Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere” (preprints/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 077 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 669efdbef9150144), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a hereditary Lipschitz submodular profile F(u, z, Y ) on z ≤ u + Y , with scalar-group Lipschitz bounds 2, 2, 1, satisfying at alignment F(u, u + Y, Y ) ≥ 2u + q∗Y, F(−aY, (1 − a)Y, Y ) = −2aY + q∗Y, ∂Y F ≥ s. (3.8) At alignment, arbitrary ellipse tests in the normalized frame are also available. For their two width depths l1, l2, the width term 2u is replaced by (1 + κ) min(l1, l2) + (1 − κ) max(l1, l2). Any additional axis label required for such a lower-bound test may be included on the measured side.
